definition_zh: 性别；社会性别；（名词的）语法性；种类（古义）
definition_en: the categories of male and female together with the social roles and identities linked to them; also a grammatical class of nouns
core_image: 同样的盒子贴着两色标签，颜色由贴标签的人决定，而不是由盒子本身决定。
scene: 图书馆的表格上，姓名之后留着一栏，填表的人可以自己决定写什么。The form leaves gender blank until the applicant chooses how to describe herself.
sceneCN: 这里 gender 指「个人在男性、女性或其他类别中的自我归属」（第 1 个义项：性别归属）；句意为表格把性别一栏留空，等申请人自己选择如何描述。可辨识物件：表格、空格、铅笔、姓名栏。

pos.zh: 性别；社会性别；语法性；种类（古义）
作定语：性别方面的，如性别角色

collocations.zh: 不分性别的；中性措辞的

gender + -ing（动名词后缀）→ 由「性别」转为「赋予性别、按性别划分的过程」
gender + -less（否定后缀）→ 由「性别」转为「无性别标记的」
gender + mis-（错误前缀）→ 由「性别」转为「错误地称呼或指认他人的性别」

senses.title: Noun class in grammar
senses.definition: one of the classes into which a language sorts nouns, often marked masculine, feminine or neuter
senses.definitionCN: 语言为名词划分的类别之一，常标为阳性、阴性或中性
senses.example: In French, gender decides whether the article is le or la.
senses.exampleCN: 在法语中，语法性别决定冠词用 le 还是 la。
senses.why: the word began as a grammar term: nouns were grouped by kind, and the groups were called genders.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是语法术语：名词按类别分组，这些组就叫语法性别。

senses.title: Socially constructed role expectations
senses.definition: the behaviour, duties and expectations a society attaches to being a man or a woman
senses.definitionCN: 社会加诸身为男性或女性的行为、职责与期待
senses.example: The study asks how gender shapes who is expected to cook at home.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究追问性别如何塑造「谁该在家做饭」的期待。
senses.why: twentieth-century scholarship separated this social layer from the older grammar term and made it the dominant sense.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪学术把这一社会层面与旧的语法术语分开，并使它成为主导义。

senses.title: Biological classification
senses.definition: the grouping of organisms as male or female by reproductive anatomy and function
senses.definitionCN: 按生殖解剖结构与功能把生物分为雄性、雌性
senses.example: Some fish change gender as they mature.
senses.exampleCN: 有些鱼在成熟过程中会改变生理性别。
senses.why: biology borrowed the word for the reproductive categories themselves, apart from social roles.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词来指生殖类别本身，与社会角色无关。

senses.title: A person's felt identity
senses.definition: the sense a person has of being male, female or another category, whether or not it matches birth records
senses.definitionCN: 个人对自身属于男性、女性或其他类别的感受，无论是否与出生记录一致
senses.example: The clinic lets patients describe their gender in their own words.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所让就诊者用自己的话描述性别认同。
senses.why: if gender is a role, then who one is as gendered cannot be read off the body alone.
senses.whyCN: 如果性别是一种角色，那么一个人作为性别主体的身份就不能只从身体读出。

senses.title: Analytical category in social science
senses.titleCN: 社会科学中的分析范畴
senses.definition: a category used to compare how resources, labour and power are distributed between men and women
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较资源、劳动与权力在男女之间如何分配的范畴
senses.example: Gender is a standard variable in studies of wages and care work.
senses.exampleCN: 在研究工资与照护劳动时，性别是一个标准变量。
senses.why: once separated from grammar, the word became a tool for measuring unequal arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 一旦与语法分开，这个词就成了衡量不平等安排的工具。

senses.title: Gender forms inside language
senses.definition: the distinctions a language makes in pronouns, agreement and titles to mark male or female reference
senses.definitionCN: 语言在代词、一致关系与称谓上为标示男性或女性所指而作出的区分
senses.example: English marks gender in pronouns but barely in nouns.
senses.exampleCN: 英语在代词上标出性别，在名词上却几乎没有。
senses.why: this sense returns to grammar but focuses on forms rather than on noun classes.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项回到语法，却聚焦于形式而非名词类别。

senses.title: Kind or sort, the old sense
senses.definition: a kind or sort of thing, the sense the word carried when it first entered English
senses.definitionCN: 事物的种类或类别，这是该词初入英语时携带的含义
senses.example: The archaic phrase all genders of goods meant every kind of merchandise.
senses.exampleCN: 古语短语「商品的所有种类」意为各类商品。
senses.why: the oldest English sense is simply kind, which is what Latin genus meant.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的义项就是种类，也就是拉丁 genus 的意思。

senses.title: A dimension in policy
senses.definition: a formal axis used to check whether rules, budgets or services affect men and women differently
senses.definitionCN: 用来检查规则、预算或服务是否对男女产生不同影响的正式维度
senses.example: Every budget line is reviewed for its gender impact.
senses.exampleCN: 每条预算项目都要审查其性别影响。
senses.why: governments turned the analytical category into an administrative checkpoint.
senses.whyCN: 政府把这一分析范畴变成了行政审查环节。

intro.en: Gender comes from Old French gendre, from Latin genus, generis 'kind, race, stock'. It entered English first as a grammar term, and the biological and social senses are twentieth-century developments. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gender 来自古法语 gendre，源于拉丁 genus、generis「种类、族类」。它初入英语时是语法术语，生理与社会义都是二十世纪的演变。年代均为约数。

items.en: genus meant 'kind, race, stock, family'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain; the older root sometimes cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: genus 意为「种类、族类、血统、家族」。其更深来源不确定；有人为它引用的更早词根属于重构形式。

items.en: generis is the genitive singular of genus; the stem gener- is the form that passed through French into English.
items.cn: generis 是 genus 的单数属格；进入法语再进入英语的正是 gener- 这个词干。

items.en: Old French gendre meant 'kind' and also named the grammatical classes of nouns; Middle English borrowed it as gendre.
items.cn: 古法语 gendre 意为「种类」，也指名词的语法类别；中古英语把它借入为 gendre。

items.en: From the fourteenth century the word was used for the masculine, feminine and neuter classes of nouns, and this remained its main sense for centuries.
items.cn: 从十四世纪起，这个词用于名词的阳性、阴性与中性类别，此后数百年间这都是它的主要义项。

items.en: The plain sense 'kind or sort' stayed in use alongside the grammar sense and is now archaic in everyday speech.
items.cn: 「种类、类别」这一朴素义与语法义长期并存，如今在日常语言中已属古旧。

items.en: The biological sense is a twentieth-century extension, and the social sense is generally thought to have spread through mid-twentieth-century psychology and sociology.
items.cn: 生理义是二十世纪的扩展；一般认为社会义经二十世纪中期心理学与社会学传播开来。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to gender but come from a different Greek or Latin branch; group two holds terms for sex and desire that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是与 gender 形近、却出自不同希腊或拉丁分支的词；第二组是常与它混淆的性、欲望相关词。

entries.definition: Coined in the early twentieth century from Greek genos 'birth, race', not from Latin genus: a unit of heredity, with no grammatical or social meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 二十世纪初据希腊 genos「出生、族类」造出，而非来自拉丁 genus：指遗传单位，没有语法或社会含义。

entries.definition: The Latin noun itself, used in biology for a rank above species; it is the direct source of gender, but it names a taxonomic class rather than a person's identity.
entries.definitionCN: 就是那个拉丁名词，生物学中用作高于物种的等级；它是 gender 的直接来源，却指分类层级，而非个人身份。

entries.definition: A French branch of the same Latin genus: a category of art or writing. It is a cousin of gender, not a synonym, and carries no idea of sex.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁 genus 的法语分支：指艺术或写作的类别。它是 gender 的表亲而非同义词，不含性别之意。

entries.definition: Latin gener- plus -ic: belonging to a whole class rather than a specific member, as in a generic drug or a generic label.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 gener- 加 -ic：属于整个类别而非特定成员，如通用药物或通用标签。

entries.definition: The biological categories of male and female, or sexual activity; gender is the social and identity layer that may or may not match it.
entries.definitionCN: 指雄雌的生理类别，或性行为；gender 是可能与之相符也可能不符的社会与认同层面。

entries.definition: A person's sexual orientation and capacity for attraction; it concerns desire, not the rank or role that gender names.
entries.definitionCN: 指个人的性取向与产生吸引的能力；它关乎欲望，而非 gender 所指的位次或角色。

entries.definition: The direction of sexual or romantic attraction; a narrower term than gender and not a category of identity in the same sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指性方面或情感方面受吸引的方向；比 gender 窄，也不是同一意义上的身份类别。

entries.definition: Prejudice or discrimination based on sex; it names a practice, while gender names the category that the practice polices.
entries.definitionCN: 基于生理性别的偏见或歧视；它命名一种做法，而 gender 命名这种做法所规训的类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin genus 'kind' became French gendre: a class, first of nouns, later of people.
normal.cn: 拉丁 genus「种类」变成法语 gendre：先是名词的类别，后来是人的类别。

normal.en: The family runs gendered, gendering, genderless, misgender, gender-neutral.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gendered、gendering、genderless、misgender、gender-neutral。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark public debate: gender equality, gender roles, gender gap.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出公共议题：性别平等、性别角色、性别差距。

normal.en: Grammar is the oldest layer: French nouns take le or la by gender.
normal.cn: 语法是最早的层面：法语名词按语法性别取 le 或 la。

normal.en: The social sense is recent, roughly mid-twentieth century, not medieval.
normal.cn: 社会义出现得晚，大约在二十世纪中期，并非中世纪产物。

abstract.en: Picture two identical boxes given different coloured labels by the person holding the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象两个一模一样的盒子，标签颜色由拿笔的人决定。

abstract.en: Picture a noun waiting at a counter to be told which line it belongs to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名词在柜台前等着被告知属于哪一队。

abstract.en: Picture a form with one blank that each person fills in their own hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，只有一个空格，每个人用自己的笔迹填写。

examples.en: The report measures the gender gap in promotions rather than in hiring.
examples.cn: 这份报告衡量的是晋升中的性别差距，而非招聘中的差距。

examples.en: Latin has three genders, and some languages have none.
examples.cn: 拉丁语有三个语法性别，有些语言则一个也没有。

examples.en: The policy treats gender as a budget dimension, not a private matter.
examples.cn: 该政策把性别当作预算维度，而非私事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gen（种类）+ der」——先给名词分种类，再给人分种类 → 语法性别、社会性别

root: 古法语 gendre < 拉丁 genus、generis「种类、族类」；原为语法术语，指名词的语法性别；生理与社会义为 20 世纪演变；genus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move, sorting into kinds: nouns are sorted by grammar, people by social expectation, bodies by biology, selves by identity, data by analysis, language by forms, old texts by the plain sense of kind, and budgets by policy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开，即分门别类：名词按语法分，人按社会期待分，身体按生理分，自我按认同分，数据按分析分，语言按形式分，古文本按「种类」的朴素义分，预算按政策分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: labels stuck onto boxes of the same shape, the colour chosen by the hand holding the label.
core.cn: 核心意象：标签贴在形状相同的盒子上，颜色由拿标签的那只手选定。

branches.en: GRAMMAR TWICE: first the class of a noun, later the forms pronouns and titles use to mark it.
branches.cn: 两次回到语法：先指名词的类别，后指代词与称谓用来标示它的一整套形式。

branches.en: ROLE AND BODY: one reading is what society expects, the other what anatomy records.
branches.cn: 角色与身体：一种读法是社会的期待，另一种读法是解剖的记录。

branches.en: SELF AND DATA: identity is felt from inside, while the analytical category is counted from outside.
branches.cn: 自我与数据：认同从内部感受，分析范畴则从外部计数。

branches.en: OLD KIND: strip away sex and grammar, and the word still means a sort of thing.
branches.cn: 古老的种类义：抽去性与语法，这个词仍然只指一类事物。

branches.en: POLICY AXIS: the category becomes a checkpoint applied to every budget line.
branches.cn: 政策轴线：这个范畴变成适用于每条预算项目的审查关卡。

intro.en: Gender is a Latin noun that came through French with almost no suffix of its own, so its family is built by adding English endings to the bare stem.
intro.cn: gender 是经法语传来的拉丁名词，本身几乎没有后缀，因此它的词族靠在裸词干上加英语词尾来构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus, generis gives the stem gener-, seen in generare and generatio; English gender, gendered, gendering, genderless and misgender all grow from that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus、generis 提供 gener- 词干，见于 generare 与 generatio；英语 gender、gendered、gendering、genderless 与 misgender 都从这个词干长出。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词指共享同一来源的一类事物。

items.meaning: of a kind, of a race

items.example: The noun names the result of the begetting.

items.meaning: kind; grammatical class; social category of sex
items.meaningCN: 种类；语法类别；社会性别
items.example: The English word kept the old sense of kind beside the grammar sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词在语法义之外保留了古老的种类义。

items.meaning: marked by or divided by gender
items.meaningCN: 带有性别标记的；按性别划分的
items.example: The division of labour in the household is strongly gendered.
items.exampleCN: 家庭中的分工带有强烈的性别色彩。

items.meaningCN: 赋予性别；按性别归类的过程
items.example: Gendering begins early in the toys children are offered.
items.exampleCN: 性别归类很早就始于给孩子的玩具。

items.example: The label uses a genderless job title.
items.exampleCN: 这个标签使用无性别指向的职位名称。

items.meaning: to refer to someone with the wrong gender

items.example: A careless form can misgender a respondent.
items.exampleCN: 一张粗心的表格可能错误指认填表人的性别。

definition_zh: 基因；遗传因子

senses.title: Unit of heredity

senses.definitionCN: 细胞中把信息从父母传给后代的组成部分
senses.example: Each gene carries a message.
senses.exampleCN: 每个基因都携带一条信息。
senses.why: This is the biological sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的生物学义项。

senses.title: Deciding factor

senses.definitionCN: 被认为决定某种特征或行为的基本因素
senses.example: The team has a gene for hard work.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍有一种勤奋的内在因素。

senses.whyCN: 生物学为与生俱来的特征提供了比喻。

items.cn: 德国科学家用 Gen 表示遗传单位。

items.en: Johannsen coined gene in English in nineteen nine.

items.en: Genetics grew as the study of genes.

sensesIntro.en: Gene is a unit of heredity, or a basic factor said to decide a quality.

definition_zh: 遗传的；基因的；与起源或发生有关的（旧义）
definition_en: relating to genes or heredity, or, in older use, relating to origin and development
core_image: 两株外观相同的幼苗被切开，内部露出一段段不同的指令条纹
scene: 两株同样的苗，一株在阴处长得细弱，一株在阳光下粗壮。The difference lies in genetic makeup rather than in care.
sceneCN: 这里 genetic 指「与基因组成有关的」（第 1 个义项：与基因相关的）；句意为差别在于基因组成，而不在于照料。可辨识物件：两株幼苗、遮阴布、光照灯、标注基因组成的卡片。

senses.title: Relating to genes
senses.definition: relating to genes or the material that carries them
senses.definitionCN: 与基因或承载基因的物质相关
senses.example: Genetic testing can reveal carrier status.
senses.exampleCN: 基因检测可以揭示携带者状态。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the whole vocabulary of heredity to a noun, so testing, material and code all become genetic.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把整套遗传词汇附着到名词上，因此检测、物质与密码都可以成为「基因的」。

senses.title: Inherited rather than acquired
senses.definition: determined by inheritance rather than by environment
senses.definitionCN: 由遗传而非环境决定
senses.example: The condition is genetic, not infectious.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病是遗传的，不是传染的。
senses.why: In this sense the word draws a line: what is genetic comes with the organism, not from contact or choice.
senses.whyCN: 在这个义项里，这个词划出一条界线：遗传之物随生物体而来，不来自接触或选择。

senses.title: Relating to origin or development
senses.titleCN: 与起源或发生有关的（旧义）
senses.definition: concerned with the origin and development of something, especially in older philosophy and linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 与某物的起源和发展有关，尤见于较早的哲学与语言学
senses.example: The genetic link between the two languages is disputed.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种语言之间的谱系联系尚有争议。
senses.why: Before genes were known, genetic meant 'pertaining to origins'; linguistics still uses it for language families.
senses.whyCN: 在基因被发现之前，genetic 意为「与起源有关的」；语言学仍用它指语言谱系。

senses.title: Of genetic engineering
senses.definition: relating to the deliberate alteration of genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 与有意改变遗传物质相关
senses.example: Genetic engineering inserted a bacterial gene into the crop.
senses.exampleCN: 基因工程把一个细菌基因植入作物。
senses.why: Once humans could cut and paste sequences, the adjective began to modify the techniques as well as the material.
senses.whyCN: 当人类能够剪切与粘贴序列后，这个形容词开始修饰技术，而不只是物质。

senses.title: Of the genetic code
senses.definition: relating to the mapping from nucleotide triplets to amino acids
senses.definitionCN: 与核苷酸三联体到氨基酸的对应关系相关
senses.example: The genetic code maps triplets to amino acids.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传密码把三联体映射到氨基酸。
senses.why: The word describes a system of correspondence, not a single gene, which is why code is its natural noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述一套对应系统，而非单个基因，因此「密码」是它的自然搭配。

senses.title: Of genetic diversity
senses.definition: relating to the range of genetic variation within a group
senses.definitionCN: 与一个群体内遗传变异的幅度相关
senses.example: Genetic diversity protects a population from disease.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传多样性保护群体免受疾病。
senses.why: Here the adjective measures variety across a group, so it contrasts with uniformity rather than with environment.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词衡量群体内的差异，因此与「一致」相对，而非与环境相对。

senses.title: Of a genetic predisposition
senses.definition: relating to an inherited tendency that raises the likelihood of a condition
senses.definitionCN: 与提高患病可能性的遗传倾向相关
senses.example: A genetic predisposition raises the risk but does not decide it.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传易感性提高风险，但不决定结果。
senses.why: The phrase keeps inheritance and inevitability apart, a distinction the adjective alone does not make.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把遗传与必然分开，而单靠形容词并不能作出这一区分。

senses.title: Of genetic relationship
senses.titleCN: 遗传关系或谱系关系的
senses.definition: relating to shared ancestry, whether of organisms or of languages
senses.definitionCN: 与共同祖先相关，无论指生物还是语言
senses.example: Genetic relationship among species is measured by shared sequences.
senses.exampleCN: 物种间的遗传关系由共享序列来测量。
senses.why: The older 'origin' sense and the newer 'gene' sense meet here: shared ancestry can be read from sequences or from language forms.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「起源」义与较新的「基因」义在此相遇：共同祖先既可从序列读出，也可从语言形式读出。

intro.en: Genetic comes from Greek genetikos 'generative', through French génétique. English first used it for 'pertaining to origin' from 1831, and from the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, for genes and heredity.
intro.cn: genetic 来自希腊 genetikos「生殖的」，经法语 génétique 传入。英语从 1831 年起用它表示「与起源有关的」，到 20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年）才用于基因与遗传。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind, birth' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so the root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类、出生」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非来源。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative' was built on genesis 'origin' with the adjectival suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的」由 genesis「起源」加形容词后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: Genetic entered English in 1831 (early nineteenth century) with the sense 'pertaining to origin or development', especially in philosophy and linguistics; the date is recorded, but how the sense developed is not fully documented.
items.cn: genetic 在 1831 年（19 世纪初）以「与起源或发展有关的」义进入英语，尤用于哲学与语言学；年代有记录，但该义如何发展并无完整文献。

items.en: From the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, the adjective was attached to genes and heredity, and this sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年），这个形容词被附着到基因与遗传上，这一义项如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: Latin genus and generare belong to the same PIE family, but genetic is not derived from them; generic is the adjective built directly on Latin genus.
items.cn: 拉丁 genus 与 generare 属于同一原始印欧语词族，但 genetic 并非由它们派生；generic 才是直接建立在拉丁 genus 上的形容词。

items.en: Source uncertain (sense dates): the 1831 first use is on record, but the exact date of the biological shift is given variously as 1905 and 1908, and no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（义项年代）：1831 年的首用有记录，但生物学义的确切年代有 1905 与 1908 两说；且 genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genetic from related formations and near sound-alikes; group two separates it from the words for inherited and whole-genome properties.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetic 与相关构词及音近词分开；第二组把它与「遗传的」「全基因组的」等词区分。

entries.definition: Built directly on Latin genus 'kind', not on Greek genetikos: it means 'general, not branded or specific'. The two words are related only through the PIE family.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建立在拉丁 genus「种类」上，而非希腊 genetikos：意为「通用的、非专属的」。两词仅通过原始印欧语词族相关联。

entries.definition: An older adjective form now mostly replaced by genetic; it survives in some technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的形容词形式，现多被 genetic 取代；仍残存于部分技术文献。

entries.definition: From genitalis, built on the same gignere stem, but it refers to reproduction and anatomy, not to genes.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 genitalis，建立在同一 gignere 词干上，但指生殖与解剖，而非基因。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus gignere 'beget': present from birth. It is not a synonym of genetic, since a congenital cause may be non-genetic.
entries.definitionCN: con-「共同」加 gignere「生育」：指出生即有。它不是 genetic 的同义词，因为先天原因未必是遗传原因。

entries.definition: It stresses descent from ancestors, while genetic points to the genes that carry the trait.
entries.definitionCN: 强调从祖先传来，而 genetic 指向承载性状的基因。

entries.definition: The ordinary participle from inherit; genetic is the technical adjective and can also mean 'relating to genes' without transmission.
entries.definitionCN: inherit 的普通分词；genetic 是技术形容词，也可仅指「与基因有关」而不涉及传递。

entries.definition: Relating to the entire genome rather than to individual genes.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个基因组相关，而非单个基因。

entries.definition: Present at birth, whether or not the cause is genetic; the two words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生时即存在，无论原因是否遗传；两词回答不同问题。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genos 'kind' + -ic: belonging to the kind one is born into.
normal.cn: genos「种类」+ -ic：属于出生所在的那个种类。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics and geneticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics 与 geneticist。

normal.en: Old sense: genetic philosophy, genetic linguistics, meaning 'of origins'.
normal.cn: 旧义搭配：发生哲学、谱系语言学，意为「关于起源的」。

normal.en: New sense in the early twentieth century: genetic code, genetic testing, genetic engineering.
normal.cn: 20 世纪初的新义搭配：遗传密码、基因检测、基因工程。

normal.en: Genetic is not congenital: a congenital condition need not be genetic.
normal.cn: genetic 不等于 congenital：先天状况未必是遗传的。

abstract.cn: 想象一个随身体附来的密封信封，无法退换。

abstract.cn: 想象两把相同的椅子，用不同批次的木材做成。

examples.cn: 有明确家族史的家庭可获得基因检测。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ tic（形容词尾）——与基因有关的 → 遗传的；旧义是「关于起源的」。

root: 希腊 genetikos「生殖的」← genesis「起源」+ genos「种族、种类」；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）；拉丁 genus 为同源词，非来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective as it moves from origins to genes: gene-related, inherited, origin-related, engineered, coded, diverse, predisposing and ancestry-sharing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形容词从「起源」走向「基因」：与基因相关、遗传而来、关于起源、经工程改造、关于密码、关于多样性、关于易感性、关于共同祖先。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical seedlings cut open to show different stripes of instructions inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：两株外观相同的幼苗被切开，内部露出不同的指令条纹。

branches.en: GENES AND INHERITANCE: the core modern pair, what genes are and what comes with them.
branches.cn: 基因与遗传：现代核心的两项，基因是什么，以及随基因而来的东西。

branches.en: ORIGINS AND ANCESTRY: the older sense survives in language families and shared descent.
branches.cn: 起源与祖先：旧义残存于语系与共同世系。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND CODE: techniques for altering sequences, and the mapping they use.
branches.cn: 工程与密码：改变序列的技术，以及它们所用的对应表。

branches.en: DIVERSITY: variation across a group, measured at the level of genes.
branches.cn: 多样性：群体内的变异，在基因层面测量。

branches.en: PREDISPOSITION: an inherited tendency that raises risk without fixing the outcome.
branches.cn: 易感性：提高风险却不固定结果的遗传倾向。

intro.en: Genetic is the adjective of the Greek-derived gen- family; its suffix marks relation, and the same stem builds the science and the agent noun.
intro.cn: genetic 是希腊来源 gen- 词族的形容词；后缀标记关系，同一词干还构成学科名与从业者名。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' gives genetic and genetics; -ikos gives the adjective, -ics the science. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty; Latin genus is only a cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」衍生 genetic 与 genetics；-ikos 构成形容词，-ics 构成学科名。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空；拉丁 genus 仅为同源词。

items.example: The stem names a kind that reproduces itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名自我繁衍的「类」。

items.example: Genesis supplies the idea of coming into being.
items.exampleCN: genesis 提供「进入存在」的观念。

items.example: The adjective described what generates.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述能生成之物。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: A gene is a unit of heredity.
items.exampleCN: 基因是遗传单位。

items.example: Genetic testing is routine.
items.exampleCN: 基因检测已很常规。

items.example: The strains are genetically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这些菌株在遗传上不同。

items.example: Genetics explains inheritance.
items.exampleCN: 遗传学解释遗传。

items.example: The geneticist mapped the region.
items.exampleCN: 这位遗传学家绘制了该区域。

items.example: The genome was sequenced.
items.exampleCN: 基因组被测序。

items.example: The genotype was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 基因型被记录。

definition_zh: 遗传上；从基因角度；以遗传方式；经基因改造地
definition_en: in a way that relates to genes or heredity, or by means of genetic material or genetic modification
core_image: 两批外观相同的种子被放进检测仪，屏幕上显示出内部不同的条带
scene: 两批种子外表相同，实验室却能测出内部的差异。The two strains are genetically distinct although they look alike.
sceneCN: 这里 genetically 指「从基因角度看、在遗传上」（第 2 个义项：就基因而言）；句意为这两个菌株虽然外表相似，在遗传上却不同。可辨识物件：两盘种子、检测仪、条带屏幕、标签。

pos.zh: 以遗传方式；经基因改造地

collocations.zh: 转基因的；经基因改造的

senses.title: By genetic modification
senses.definition: by changing genetic material, especially through engineering
senses.definitionCN: 通过改变遗传物质，尤指通过工程手段
senses.example: The crop was genetically modified to resist insects.
senses.exampleCN: 这种作物经过基因改造以抵抗昆虫。
senses.why: The adverb marks the means, so genetically modified means changed at the level of the instructions rather than by breeding alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记手段，因此「经基因改造」指在指令层面被改变，而非仅靠育种。

senses.title: In genetic terms
senses.definition: as judged by genes rather than by appearance
senses.definitionCN: 以基因而非外表来评判
senses.example: The two strains are genetically distinct although they look alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个菌株外表相似，在遗传上却不同。
senses.why: Here the adverb sets the viewpoint: what is compared is the sequence, not the visible form.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个副词设定视角：比较的是序列，而非可见形态。

senses.title: As determined by inheritance
senses.definition: in a way that is influenced or fixed by inherited factors
senses.definitionCN: 受遗传因素影响或固定的方式
senses.example: Height is genetically influenced but not fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 身高受遗传影响，但并非固定不变。
senses.why: The adverb can soften causation: genetically influenced leaves room for environment, while genetically determined closes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以缓和因果关系：受遗传影响仍给环境留余地，而由遗传决定则不留。

senses.title: At the level of genetic material
senses.definition: by examining or acting on DNA or other hereditary material
senses.definitionCN: 通过检查或作用于遗传物质
senses.example: The samples were compared genetically.
senses.exampleCN: 这些样本在遗传层面做了比较。
senses.why: The adverb can describe a method as well as a cause: comparing genetically means using sequences as the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词既能描述方法也能描述原因：在遗传层面比较，就是用序列作证据。

senses.title: Through genetic transmission
senses.definition: by passing from parents to offspring through genes
senses.definitionCN: 通过基因由亲代传给子代
senses.example: The disorder is genetically transmitted.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病经遗传传递。
senses.why: The adverb attaches transmission to genes, so the route is explicitly biological rather than social.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把传递附着到基因上，因此路径明确是生物的，而非社会的。

senses.title: With respect to genetic makeup
senses.definition: in terms of the overall genetic constitution of a group
senses.definitionCN: 就一个群体的整体遗传构成而言
senses.example: Genetically, the island population is unusually uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 就遗传而言，这个岛屿群体异常一致。
senses.why: At the start of a clause, the adverb frames the whole statement as a genetic judgement.
senses.whyCN: 置于句首时，这个副词把整句框定为遗传判断。

senses.title: By genetic engineering
senses.definition: by deliberate insertion, deletion or editing of sequences
senses.definitionCN: 通过有意插入、删除或编辑序列
senses.example: The vaccine seed strain was genetically engineered.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗种株经过基因工程改造。
senses.why: Engineering is the most deliberate form of the means sense: the change is designed, not selected from existing variation.
senses.whyCN: 工程是手段义中最有意的一种：改变是被设计出来的，而非从既有变异中选出的。

senses.title: In genetic classification
senses.definition: as grouped by shared genetic material rather than by visible traits
senses.definitionCN: 按共享遗传物质而非可见性状来归类
senses.example: Genetically, the two species belong to one genus.
senses.exampleCN: 从遗传分类看，这两个物种属于同一属。
senses.why: The adverb can qualify taxonomy itself, marking a classification that follows sequences instead of shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词能限定分类学本身，标记一种依据序列而非外形的分类。

intro.en: Genetically is genetic plus the adverbial ending -ally, from -al + -ly. The adjective goes back through French to Greek genetikos 'generative'.
intro.cn: genetically 是 genetic 加副词词尾 -ally 构成，后者来自 -al + -ly。形容词经法语上溯到希腊 genetikos「生殖的」。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so the root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非来源。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative' was formed from genesis 'origin' with the suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的」由 genesis「起源」加后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: Genetic entered English in 1831 for 'pertaining to origin', and from the early twentieth century, often dated 1908, for genes; genetical was the older adjective form.
items.cn: genetic 在 1831 年以「关于起源的」义进入英语，20 世纪初（常定在 1908 年）起用于基因；genetical 是较早的形容词形式。

items.en: The adverb was built as genetic + -al + -ly, giving genetically; the older genetical now survives mainly in technical writing.
items.cn: 副词由 genetic + -al + -ly 构成，写作 genetically；较旧的 genetical 如今主要残存于技术文献。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adverb spread to modification, screening and classification: genetically modified, genetically screened, genetically distinct.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个副词扩展到改造、筛查与分类：转基因、经基因筛查、遗传上不同。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first recorded use of the adverb is not firmly dated, and no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个副词的最早书证没有确切年代，且 genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genetically from look-alikes with other roots; group two separates it from adverbs that name inheritance, genotype or environment.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetically 与词根不同的形近词分开；第二组把它与表示遗传、基因型或环境的副词区分。

entries.definition: From Latin genialis 'festive, natural', connected with genius, not genos: in a cheerful and friendly way.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 genialis「节庆的、天生的」，与 genius 相关，而非 genos：指和蔼愉快地。

entries.definition: From general, built on Latin genus 'kind' but meaning 'in most cases'; it is not a genetic judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 general，虽建立在拉丁 genus「种类」上，但意为「通常」；不是遗传判断。

entries.definition: The most common collocation, naming an organism whose material has been deliberately altered.
entries.definitionCN: 最常见的搭配，指遗传物质被有意改造过的生物。

entries.definition: Sharing the same genetic material, as clones do; the adverb marks the level of identity.
entries.definitionCN: 共享相同遗传物质，如克隆体；副词标记同一性的层面。

entries.definition: It stresses transmission from ancestors, while genetically can also mean 'at the level of genes' without descent.
entries.definitionCN: 强调从祖先传递，而 genetically 也可仅指「在基因层面」，不涉及世系。

entries.definition: Relating to the inherited constitution at one or more loci, a narrower technical term.
entries.definitionCN: 与一个或多个位点的遗传组成相关，是更窄的技术词。

entries.definition: Relating to visible or measurable traits, the opposite angle from genetically.
entries.definitionCN: 与可见或可测性状相关，角度与 genetically 相反。

entries.definition: Relating to external conditions rather than genes; the usual contrast in nature-nurture debates.
entries.definitionCN: 与外部条件相关而非基因；是天性与教养争论中的常见对照。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genetic + -al + -ly: in the manner of genes.
normal.cn: genetic + -al + -ly：以基因的方式。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics and geneticist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics 与 geneticist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: genetically modified, genetically distinct, genetically determined.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：转基因的、遗传上不同的、由遗传决定的。

normal.en: As a sentence opener, genetically frames the whole claim.
normal.cn: 作为句首状语，genetically 为整句断言设定框架。

normal.en: Genetically is not environmentally: the two adverbs split nature from nurture.
normal.cn: genetically 与 environmentally 相对：两个副词把天性从教养中分开。

abstract.en: Picture two jars with identical labels but different contents.
abstract.cn: 想象两个标签相同、内容不同的罐子。

abstract.en: Picture a barcode read while the package looks blank.
abstract.cn: 想象包装看似空白，条形码却已被读出。

abstract.en: Picture a family resemblance measured with a ruler instead of an eye.
abstract.cn: 想象用尺子而不是眼睛来测量家族相似。

examples.en: The tomatoes were genetically modified to ripen on schedule.
examples.cn: 这些番茄经过基因改造，可按计划成熟。

examples.en: Genetically, the two populations have been separate for centuries.
examples.cn: 从遗传上看，这两个群体已分离数百年。

examples.en: The rescued cubs are genetically diverse enough to breed.
examples.cn: 获救的幼兽遗传多样性足够，可以繁育。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ tically（副词尾）——从基因角度 → 遗传上；与「转基因的」搭配时指经基因改造。

root: genetic + -al + -ly；genetic 来自希腊 genetikos「生殖的」← genos「种族、种类」；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one viewpoint: by modification, in genetic terms, by inheritance, at the material level, through transmission, as makeup, by engineering and in classification.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个视角展开：经改造、从基因角度、由遗传决定、在物质层面、经传递、就组成而言、经工程、在分类上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two trays of identical seeds, while a screen shows different internal bands.
core.cn: 核心意象：两盘外观相同的种子，屏幕却显示出不同的内部条带。

branches.en: BY MODIFICATION: the change is made deliberately at the level of the instructions.
branches.cn: 经改造：改变是在指令层面有意作出的。

branches.en: VIEWPOINT: the judgement is made by sequences rather than by appearance or shape.
branches.cn: 视角：判断依据序列而非外表或形态。

branches.en: CAUSE AND ROUTE: inherited influence, and transmission from parents to offspring.
branches.cn: 原因与路径：遗传影响，以及由亲代到子代的传递。

branches.en: MATERIAL LEVEL: the comparison or action occurs on the hereditary material itself.
branches.cn: 物质层面：比较或作用发生在遗传物质本身。

branches.en: MAKEUP: the adverb frames a statement about a group's overall constitution.
branches.cn: 组成：副词为关于群体整体构成的陈述设定框架。

intro.en: Genetically is a layered adverb: a Greek-derived stem, an adjective suffix, and a further adverbial ending.
intro.cn: genetically 是分层构成的副词：希腊来源词干、形容词后缀，再加副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos gives gene and genetic; -ic and -al form the adjective, and -ly forms the adverb. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos 衍生 gene 与 genetic；-ic 与 -al 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

definition_zh: 遗传学；（某生物或群体的）遗传组成
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies heredity and genes, or the genetic makeup of an organism or group
core_image: 一块白板写满杂交组合与比例，旁边摆着一排标了代号的育苗盘
scene: 实验室的白板上写满杂交组合，研究生在计算下一代的性状比例。Modern genetics explains how traits pass from parents to offspring.
sceneCN: 这里 genetics 指「研究遗传与基因的生物学科」（第 1 个义项：遗传学）；句意为现代遗传学解释了性状如何由亲代传给子代。可辨识物件：白板、粉笔、杂交组合表、育苗盘、计算器。

pos.zh: 遗传组成；遗传特征（作复数）

senses.title: The science of heredity
senses.definition: the branch of biology concerned with genes, heredity and variation
senses.definitionCN: 研究基因、遗传与变异的生物学分支
senses.example: Modern genetics explains how traits pass from parents to offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 现代遗传学解释了性状如何由亲代传给子代。
senses.why: The name was coined for a discipline, so genetics takes a singular verb even though it ends in -s.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称是为学科而造的，因此尽管以 -s 结尾，genetics 仍接单数动词。

senses.title: The genetic makeup of an organism
senses.definition: the total genetic constitution of an organism or group
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物或群体的全部遗传构成
senses.example: The genetics of this population differ from those of the mainland.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体的遗传组成与大陆群体不同。
senses.why: Because the field studies variation, its name was transferred to the variation itself, especially in population studies.
senses.whyCN: 由于该领域研究变异，其名称被转用到变异本身，尤其在群体研究中。

senses.title: A branch or subfield
senses.definition: a specialized division of the science, such as medical or molecular genetics
senses.definitionCN: 该学科的一个专门分支，如医学遗传学或分子遗传学
senses.example: Medical genetics now guides many cancer treatments.
senses.exampleCN: 医学遗传学如今指导许多癌症治疗。
senses.why: Compound names such as medical genetics treat the word as a countable field, so one can speak of several genetics.
senses.whyCN: 医学遗传学这类复合名称把该词当作可数的领域，因此可以说有多个遗传学分支。

senses.title: Molecular genetics
senses.definition: the study of how genetic material is copied, expressed and repaired at the molecular level
senses.definitionCN: 在分子层面研究遗传物质如何复制、表达与修复
senses.example: Molecular genetics studies how sequences are copied and repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 分子遗传学研究序列如何被复制与修复。
senses.why: When the focus moves to molecules, the word pairs with an adjective that names the level rather than the organism.
senses.whyCN: 当焦点转向分子，这个词便与标明层次的形容词搭配，而非与生物体搭配。

senses.title: Population genetics
senses.definition: the study of allele frequencies and their changes in populations
senses.definitionCN: 研究群体中等位基因频率及其变化
senses.example: Population genetics tracks allele frequencies over time.
senses.exampleCN: 群体遗传学追踪等位基因频率随时间的变化。
senses.why: Once genes are counted across groups, genetics becomes a science of frequencies rather than of single families.
senses.whyCN: 一旦跨群体计数基因，遗传学就成为频率的科学，而非单个家族的科学。

senses.title: Genetics as a subject taught
senses.definition: the subject as taught or examined in a course
senses.definitionCN: 作为课程或考试科目的遗传学
senses.example: She teaches genetics to first-year biology students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给一年级生物学生教遗传学。
senses.why: The discipline name also names a course, which is why it appears with teach, study and examine.
senses.whyCN: 学科名同时也指一门课程，因此常与「教」「学」「考」搭配。

senses.title: Clinical genetics
senses.definition: the application of genetics to diagnosis and counselling in medicine
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学在医学诊断与咨询中的应用
senses.example: Clinical genetics offers testing for inherited conditions.
senses.exampleCN: 临床遗传学为遗传性疾病提供检测。
senses.why: The clinical compound marks the point where the science meets patients, testing and advice.
senses.whyCN: 临床复合词标记出这门科学与患者、检测与建议相接的地方。

senses.title: Genetics in agriculture
senses.definition: the use of genetic knowledge to improve crops and livestock
senses.definitionCN: 利用遗传知识改良作物与家畜
senses.example: Modern genetics produced wheat that tolerates drought.
senses.exampleCN: 现代遗传学培育出了耐旱小麦。
senses.why: Breeding was practiced long before the science existed, but genetics now explains and directs what breeders do.
senses.whyCN: 育种远在这门科学出现之前就已实践，但遗传学如今解释并指导育种者的工作。

intro.en: Genetics was coined from Greek genetikos 'generative', a derivative of genesis 'origin' and genos 'race, kind'. The English noun is usually credited to William Bateson, who proposed it in 1905 and published it in 1906; other reference works record an isolated use in 1872 and a related sense in 1891, so the first date is disputed.
intro.cn: genetics 由希腊 genetikos「生殖的、产生的」造出，后者源出 genesis「起源」与 genos「种族、种类」。英语名词通常归功于威廉·贝特森，他于 1905 年提出、1906 年发表；另有参考书记录 1872 年的一处孤立用法与 1891 年的相关义，因此首见年代存在争议。

items.en: Genos meant 'race, kind, birth'. It belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-, so that root form is a reconstruction; Latin genus is a cognate, not the source of the English word.
items.cn: genos 意为「种族、种类、出生」。它属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族，因此该词根形式是重构；拉丁 genus 是同源词，并非这个英语词的来源。

items.en: Genesis 'origin, generation' supplied the noun of coming into being that stands behind genetikos.
items.cn: genesis「起源、生成」提供了「进入存在」的名词，位于 genetikos 之后。

items.en: Genetikos 'generative, concerned with generation' was formed with the adjectival suffix -ikos.
items.cn: genetikos「生殖的、与生成有关的」由形容词后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: William Bateson proposed genetics in a letter of 1905 and used it in print in 1906; some reference works record an isolated 1872 use and a 'study of heredity' sense in 1891, so the exact first appearance is disputed rather than the root.
items.cn: 威廉·贝特森在 1905 年的一封信中提出 genetics，并于 1906 年用于印刷文本；有些参考书记录 1872 年的一处孤立用法与 1891 年的「遗传研究」义，因此存疑的是确切首见年代，而非词根。

items.en: During the twentieth century the field split into molecular, population and clinical branches, and the plural-looking name stayed grammatically singular.
items.cn: 20 世纪，该领域分化为分子、群体与临床分支，这个看似复数的名称在语法上仍保持单数。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the root in genetikos is not in doubt, but the first English appearance is disputed between an isolated 1872 use, an 1891 sense and Bateson's 1905-1906 coinage; no Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty, and the Latin cognate genus belongs to the same PIE family but is not the source.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：genetikos 的词根并无疑问，但英语首见年代在 1872 年孤立用法、1891 年义项与贝特森 1905—1906 年造词之间存在争议；genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空；拉丁同源词 genus 属于同一原始印欧语词族，但并非来源。

note.en: Group one separates genetics from words built on the same Greek stem and from one accidental sound-alike; group two separates it from the neighbouring sciences and from the older word for transmission.
note.cn: 第一组把 genetics 与同一希腊词干构成的词及一个偶然音近词分开；第二组把它与邻近学科及更早的「传递」用词区分。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'relating to genes'; genetics is the discipline or the makeup it studies.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与基因有关的」的形容词；genetics 是学科或被研究的组成。

entries.definition: The study of whole genomes rather than single genes; it grew out of genetics but is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个基因组而非单个基因的学科；由遗传学发展而来，但并非同义词。

entries.definition: The unit of heredity that genetics studies; the science and its object are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 遗传学所研究的遗传单位；学科与其对象不能互换。

entries.definition: From Greek gymnazein 'to train naked', not from genos: physical exercises. The resemblance is only in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 gymnazein「裸身训练」，并非 genos：指体操。相似仅在读音。

entries.definition: The transmission of traits; genetics is the science that explains it, not the transmission itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指性状传递；genetics 是解释它的科学，而非传递本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for property and biological transmission; genetics names the discipline, not an estate.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖财产与生物传递的较宽泛词；genetics 命名学科，而非产业。

entries.definition: The study of complete genomes; genetics often focuses on individual genes and their effects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究完整基因组的学科；genetics 常聚焦单个基因及其效应。

entries.definition: The wider study of biological molecules; genetics is one part of it, focused on heredity.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物大分子的更广领域；遗传学是其中专注遗传的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' + -etics: the study of how kind passes down.
normal.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」+ 学科后缀：研究种类如何下传的学问。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genetic, genetically, genetics, geneticist and genomics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genetic、genetically、genetics、geneticist 与 genomics。

normal.en: The name ends in -s but takes a singular verb when it means the science.
normal.cn: 这个词以 -s 结尾，但指学科时接单数动词。

normal.en: Bateson proposed the term in 1905 and printed it in 1906.
normal.cn: 贝特森于 1905 年提出该术语，1906 年正式印行。

normal.en: Medical, molecular and population are its common branches.
normal.cn: 医学、分子与群体是其常见分支。

abstract.en: Picture a library that catalogues not books but the instructions for making them.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆不编目书籍，而编目造书的指令。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree redrawn as a table of frequencies.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树被重画成一张频率表。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe book whose pages are copied with occasional mistakes.
abstract.cn: 想象一本食谱，页面被复制时偶尔出错。

examples.en: Genetics has become central to conservation planning.
examples.cn: 遗传学已成为保护规划的核心。

examples.en: The genetics of the island population show a long isolation.
examples.cn: 这个岛屿群体的遗传组成显示出长期隔离。

examples.en: She switched from field biology to genetics after her first course.
examples.cn: 她在上完第一门课后从野外生物学转向遗传学。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ tics（学科）——研究基因的学科 → 遗传学；指学科时作单数。

root: 希腊 genetikos「生殖的」← genesis「起源」+ genos「种族、种类」；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）；拉丁 genus 为同源词，非来源；英语词通常归功于贝特森 1905—1906 年，另有 1872/1891 年早期用法之说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one discipline as it spreads: the science, the makeup it describes, its branches, its molecular and population scales, its teaching, its clinical use and its agricultural use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一门学科的外扩展开：学科本身、它所描述的组成、它的分支、分子与群体尺度、它的教学、临床用途与农业用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whiteboard of crosses and ratios beside trays of labelled seedlings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写满杂交与比例的白板，旁边是一排标了代号的育苗盘。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: the science itself, including the course that teaches it.
branches.cn: 学科：科学本身，包括讲授它的课程。

branches.en: THE MAKEUP: the name transferred from the field to what the field measures.
branches.cn: 组成：名称从领域转用到领域所测量的对象。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND SCALES: medical, molecular and population divisions.
branches.cn: 分支与尺度：医学、分子与群体划分。

branches.en: CLINICAL USE: testing and counselling where the science meets patients.
branches.cn: 临床用途：科学与患者相接处的检测与咨询。

branches.en: AGRICULTURAL USE: breeding guided by genetic knowledge.
branches.cn: 农业用途：由遗传知识指导的育种。

intro.en: Genetics is a Greek-derived compound whose stem also builds the modern vocabulary of heredity; the suffixes mark an adjective, a science and a person.
intro.cn: genetics 是希腊语来源的复合词，其词干还构成现代遗传词汇；后缀分别标记形容词、学科与从业者。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos 'race, kind' gives gene, genetic, genetics and genomics; -ikos gives the adjective and -ics names the field. No Latin derivative of genetikos exists, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」衍生 gene、genetic、genetics 与 genomics；-ikos 构成形容词，-ics 命名学科。genetikos 没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: The stem names a kind that reproduces its kind.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名会繁衍同类的那种「类」。

items.example: Genesis names the coming-into-being of a thing.
items.exampleCN: genesis 命名事物进入存在的过程。

items.example: The adjective described what produces or transmits.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述能产生或传递的东西。

items.example: The suffix turned the noun stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词词干变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix makes the adjective into a science name.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成学科名。

items.example: A gene is a unit of heredity.
items.exampleCN: 基因是遗传单位。

items.example: Genetic testing is now routine.
items.exampleCN: 基因检测如今已很常规。

items.example: The strains are genetically distinct.
items.exampleCN: 这些菌株在遗传上不同。

items.example: Genetics explains inheritance.
items.exampleCN: 遗传学解释遗传。

items.example: The geneticist mapped the region.
items.exampleCN: 这位遗传学家绘制了该区域。

items.example: Genomics compares complete sequences.
items.exampleCN: 基因组学比较完整序列。

items.example: The genotype was recorded for each plant.
items.exampleCN: 每株植物都记录了基因型。

definition_zh: 基因组；一套完整的遗传物质
definition_en: the complete set of genetic material in a cell, organism or species
core_image: 一份厚得像电话簿的目录，里面装着构成一个身体所需的全部指令
scene: 把一个人的全部遗传指令装进一份目录，厚得像电话簿。The human genome contains every instruction needed to build a body.
sceneCN: 这里 genome 指「一个生物体或物种的全套遗传物质」（第 1 个义项：完整的遗传物质集合）；句意为人类基因组包含构建一个身体所需的全部指令。可辨识物件：厚目录、索引标签、染色体示意图、书签。

senses.title: The complete genetic material
senses.definition: the entire set of genetic material in a cell or organism
senses.definitionCN: 细胞或生物体内全部遗传物质的总和
senses.example: The human genome contains every instruction needed to build a body.
senses.exampleCN: 人类基因组包含构建一个身体所需的全部指令。
senses.why: The word was coined for the whole set, so its core sense is collective: one genome per cell or species, not one per trait.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是为「整套」而造的，因此核心义是集合性的：每个细胞或物种一个基因组，而不是每个性状一个。

senses.title: A sequenced genome
senses.definition: the genome of an organism as read out in sequence data
senses.definitionCN: 以序列数据形式读出的某生物基因组
senses.example: The first genome of a fruit fly was published in 2000.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇的第一个基因组于 2000 年公布。
senses.why: Once sequencing became possible, the word came to mean the published read-out as well as the biological set.
senses.whyCN: 当测序成为可能后，这个词既指生物学的集合，也指公布的读出结果。

senses.title: A genome as a dataset
senses.definition: a collection of sequences from many individuals used for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较的、来自许多个体的序列集合
senses.example: Researchers compared genomes from a thousand patients.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者比较了一千名患者的基因组。
senses.why: In data work the singular expands to many files: a 'genome' can mean the assembled dataset of one individual.
senses.whyCN: 在数据工作中，单数扩展到许多文件：一个「基因组」可指某个体组装好的数据集。

senses.title: A viral genome
senses.definition: the genetic material of a virus, often a single RNA or DNA molecule
senses.definitionCN: 病毒的遗传物质，常为单个核糖核酸或脱氧核糖核酸分子
senses.example: The viral genome is only a few thousand units long.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒基因组只有几千个单位长。
senses.why: Viruses have genomes too, so the term crosses the boundary between cellular life and its parasites.
senses.whyCN: 病毒也有基因组，因此这个术语跨越了细胞生命与其寄生者的边界。

senses.title: Genome organization
senses.definition: the way genetic material is arranged and packed in a cell
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质在细胞中排列与包装的方式
senses.example: The genome is packed into chromosomes.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组被包装进染色体。
senses.why: The word can name the arrangement, not only the contents, which is why genomes have sizes and structures.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能命名排列方式，而不只是内容，因此基因组有大小与结构。

senses.title: A genome project
senses.definition: a large coordinated effort to sequence a species' genome
senses.definitionCN: 为测定某一物种基因组而进行的大型协作
senses.example: The genome project finished ahead of schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 这项基因组计划提前完成。
senses.why: Big science turned the word into a project name, so 'the genome' can mean the effort as well as the object.
senses.whyCN: 大科学把这个词变成项目名，因此「基因组」也可指这项工程，而不只是对象。

senses.title: Genome size
senses.definition: the total amount of genetic material in a genome, often measured in base pairs
senses.definitionCN: 基因组中遗传物质的总量，常以碱基对计量
senses.example: Genome size does not track organism complexity.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组大小并不随生物复杂度变化。
senses.why: Measuring a genome requires treating it as a quantity, which produces the size sense.
senses.whyCN: 测量基因组需要把它当作一个量，于是产生「大小」这一义。

senses.title: A target for genome editing
senses.definition: the whole set of material that can be altered at precise sites
senses.definitionCN: 可在精确位点被改变的全部遗传物质
senses.example: The genome can now be edited at precise sites.
senses.exampleCN: 基因组如今可以在精确位点被编辑。
senses.why: Editing acts on the set rather than on one gene, so the word names the scope of the intervention.
senses.whyCN: 编辑作用于整套而非单个基因，因此这个词命名干预的范围。

intro.en: Genome was coined by Hans Winkler in 1920 as German Genom, usually explained as a blend of Gen 'gene' and Chromosom 'chromosome'.
intro.cn: genome 由汉斯·温克勒于 1920 年以德语 Genom 造出，通常解释为 Gen「基因」与 Chromosom「染色体」的混成词。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-; the root form is a reconstruction, and Latin genus is a cognate rather than the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族；该词根形式是重构，拉丁 genus 是同源词而非来源。

items.en: The suffix -ome, extracted from chromosome, marks a complete set. Chromosome itself joins Greek chroma 'colour' and soma 'body'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ome 从 chromosome 中析出，标记一个完整集合。chromosome 本身由希腊 chroma「颜色」与 soma「身体」构成。

items.en: Hans Winkler coined German Genom in 1920; it is generally considered a blend of Gen and Chromosom, though that reading remains an interpretation of his intention.
items.cn: 汉斯·温克勒于 1920 年造出德语 Genom；一般认为它是 Gen 与 Chromosom 的混成，但这一读法仍是对其意图的解释。

items.en: English genome is recorded by 1930 and spread widely later in the twentieth century with sequencing projects; the first English citation is often dated to that year.
items.cn: 英语 genome 在 1930 年前已有记录，20 世纪后期随测序计划广泛传播；最早的英语书证常定在该年。

items.en: The meaning widened from a set of genes to the entire sequence of a cell or species, including non-coding regions.
items.cn: 词义从「一组基因」扩展到细胞或物种的全部序列，包括非编码区域。

items.en: Source uncertain (coinage details): the 1920 date is documented, but the blend account is an interpretation, and the pre-Latin root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（造词细节）：1920 年这一年代有文献可查，但混成说法属于解释，且拉丁语之前的词根形式是重构。

note.en: Group one separates genome from same-root terms and one accidental sound-alike; group two separates it from the neighbouring whole-set and carrier terms.
note.cn: 第一组把 genome 与同根词及一个偶然音近词分开；第二组把它与相邻的「整套」和「载体」术语区分。

entries.definition: One segment of instructions; a genome is the complete set of such segments.
entries.definitionCN: 指一段指令；基因组是这类片段的完整集合。

entries.definition: The inherited constitution at one or more loci; a genome is the whole material, not a combination at a locus.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个或多个位点的遗传组成；基因组是全部物质，而非某位点的组合。

entries.definition: The study of genomes; genome is the object, genomics is the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究基因组的学科；genome 是对象，genomics 是学科。

entries.definition: A garden ornament or a folklore figure; its origin is not related to genos. The resemblance is only in spelling and sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指花园装饰或民间传说人物；其来源与 genos 无关。相似仅在拼写与读音。

entries.definition: A structure that carries part of the genome; a genome is the total material, packaged into chromosomes.
entries.definitionCN: 承载部分基因组的结构；基因组是被包装进染色体的全部物质。

entries.definition: The inherited constitution, especially at specified loci; the genome is the full sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指遗传组成，尤指特定位点；基因组是完整序列。

entries.definition: The set of all RNA transcripts; it is a subset of what the genome contains, not the genome itself.
entries.definitionCN: 全部核糖核酸转录本的集合；是基因组内容的一部分，而非基因组本身。

entries.definition: The complete set of proteins produced; it is downstream of the genome and not the same object.
entries.definitionCN: 所产生的全部蛋白质集合；位于基因组下游，并非同一对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: gene + -ome: the whole set of genes.
normal.cn: gene + -ome：全部基因的集合。

normal.en: The family runs gene, genome, genomic, genomics and genotype.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gene、genome、genomic、genomics 与 genotype。

normal.en: Winkler coined Genom in 1920 as gene plus chromosome.
normal.cn: 温克勒于 1920 年以 gene 加 chromosome 造出 Genom。

normal.en: Genome size is measured in base pairs, not in gene counts.
normal.cn: 基因组大小以碱基对计量，而非以基因数计量。

normal.en: Genomics is the science; the genome is its object.
normal.cn: genomics 是学科；genome 是它的对象。

abstract.en: Picture a phone book that contains every instruction for building a city.
abstract.cn: 想象一本电话簿，装着建造一座城市所需的全部指令。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf treated as one catalogue entry.
abstract.cn: 想象整排书架被当作一条目录记录。

abstract.en: Picture a map that includes empty streets as well as named ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，既有命名街道，也有空白街道。

examples.en: The genome was assembled from millions of short reads.
examples.cn: 这个基因组由数百万条短读段组装而成。

examples.en: Viral genomes mutate faster than most cellular genomes.
examples.cn: 病毒基因组比多数细胞基因组突变得更快。

examples.en: Genome size varies widely among flowering plants.
examples.cn: 开花植物的基因组大小差异很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: gene（基因）+ ome（整体）——全部基因装在一起 → 基因组；-ome 来自 chromosome。

root: 德语 Genom（温克勒，1920）＝Gen「基因」+ Chromosom「染色体」的混成；gen 源于希腊 genos「种族、种类」，genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one complete set: the material, its sequenced read-out, its data form, its viral version, its packing, its project, its size and its edited scope.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个完整集合展开：物质本身、测序读出、数据形式、病毒版本、包装方式、计划、大小与可编辑范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a phone-book-thick catalogue holding every instruction for a body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本电话簿厚的目录，装着构建一个身体所需的全部指令。

branches.en: THE WHOLE SET: all the material, and the way it is packed.

definition_zh: 属；（生物分类的）属；逻辑上的属；一类
definition_en: a rank in biological classification above species and below family, or a class that contains subordinate kinds
core_image: 同一排标本盒里装着几种相似的动物，盒盖写着它们共用的名称
scene: 同一属里的几种猫科动物被排在同一排标本盒中，盒盖上写着它们共用的名称。 Several cat species of the same genus are arranged in one row of specimen boxes, with their shared name written on the lids.
sceneCN: 这里 genus 是「属」（第 1 个义项：位于种之上、科之下的分类阶元）；句意：同一属里的几种猫科动物被排在同一排标本盒中，盒盖上写着它们共用的名称。

pos.zh: 属（复数 genera）；逻辑上的属；一类

senses.title: The rank above species
senses.definition: the taxonomic rank that groups one or more species sharing a common ancestor and a set of structural features
senses.definitionCN: 把共享祖先与一组结构特征的一个或多个物种聚合起来的分类阶元
senses.example: The genus contains four species, two of them recently described.
senses.exampleCN: 这个属包含四个物种，其中两个是最近描述的。
senses.why: Latin genus meant 'birth, race, kind'; taxonomy kept 'kind' and gave it a fixed position: a kind that holds smaller kinds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 genus 意为「出生、族类、种类」；分类学保留了「种类」义，并给它固定位置：一个装更小种类的种类。

senses.title: The first word of a binomial
senses.definition: the capitalized element placed first in the two-part scientific name of a species
senses.definitionCN: 物种两段式学名中置于最前、首字母大写的成分
senses.example: The genus name is capitalized and may be abbreviated after first use.
senses.exampleCN: 属名首字母大写，首次出现之后可以缩写。
senses.why: A binomial is an address written in two words, and the genus is the street while the species epithet is the house.
senses.whyCN: 双名法是用两个词写成的地址：属名是街道，种加词是门牌。

senses.title: The logical genus containing species
senses.definition: in logic, a wider class that contains narrower classes as its species, the relation of genus and species
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑学中作为种的上位、包含较窄类别的较宽类别，即属与种的关系
senses.example: Animal is the genus and bird the species in the old scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧方案中，动物是属，鸟是种。
senses.why: Logic had the pair before biology: genus and species named containment, and Linnaeus borrowed a ready-made ladder.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学早于生物学拥有这对词：属与种表示包含关系，林奈借用的是一架现成的梯子。

senses.title: A kind or class in general
senses.definition: a broad kind of thing, often in the phrase a genus of, where the reference is not biological
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛的一类事物，常用于 a genus of 结构，所指并非生物
senses.example: A genus of problems resisted every standard method.
senses.exampleCN: 有一类问题抵抗所有标准方法。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the Latin breadth: any class that holds smaller classes can be called a genus, with or without specimens.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留了拉丁语的宽度：任何容纳更小类别的类别都可以叫 genus，与标本无关。

senses.title: The plural genera
senses.definition: the Latin third-declension plural, used in English for several genera and often a marker of technical writing
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁第三变格法复数，英语中用来指多个属，也常成为技术写作的标志
senses.example: Three genera were moved into the new family.
senses.exampleCN: 三个属被移入新科。
senses.why: English keeps genera because the Latin plural is fixed in the codes; using genuses marks a speaker as an outsider.
senses.whyCN: 英语保留 genera，因为法规固定了拉丁复数；说 genuses 会显出外行。

senses.title: The type genus of a family
senses.definition: the genus that gives a family its name and fixes the application of that family name
senses.definitionCN: 为某科提供名称、并固定该科名适用范围的那个属
senses.example: The family takes its name from the type genus.
senses.exampleCN: 这个科的名字取自其模式属。
senses.why: Names must be anchored somewhere, and the type genus is that anchor: the family name is built from it and cannot drift away.
senses.whyCN: 名称必须有锚点，模式属就是那个锚：科名由它构成，因此不能漂移。

senses.title: A monotypic genus
senses.definition: a genus that contains only one species, so the genus and the species carry almost the same content
senses.definitionCN: 只含一个物种的属，属与种的内容因此几乎相同
senses.example: The monotypic genus has no second species to compare with.
senses.exampleCN: 这个单型属没有第二个物种可供比较。
senses.why: When a genus holds one species, the rank above adds no information; taxonomists argue whether such genera should be kept.
senses.whyCN: 当一个属只含一个物种时，上一级并不增加信息；分类学家因此争论这样的属是否应当保留。

senses.title: The adjective generic and its drift
senses.titleCN: 派生形容词 generic 的语义漂移
senses.definition: the derived adjective meaning 'of a genus', which has also come to mean 'common to a whole class' and hence 'unbranded'
senses.definitionCN: 派生形容词，意为「属的」，又引申为「整类共有的」，进而指「无品牌的」
senses.example: Generic names on the shelf told the shopper nothing about the maker.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上的通用名称没有告诉顾客任何关于厂家的事。
senses.why: From 'of a kind' to 'shared by the whole kind' to 'having no distinctive mark': the drift is visible in the word generic, not in genus itself.
senses.whyCN: 从「某一类的」到「整类共有的」再到「没有独特标记的」：这一漂移体现在 generic 一词中，而非 genus 本身。

intro.en: Genus is a Latin noun taken into English with its Latin plural genera. It meant 'birth, origin, race, kind' and became the rank above species. Dates are approximate, and the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
intro.cn: genus 是连同拉丁复数 genera 一起进入英语的拉丁名词，意为「出生、起源、族类、种类」，后来成为物种之上的阶元。年代为约数，印欧词根属重构。

items.en: Genus, generis meant 'birth, descent, race, kind'. It was a third-declension neuter noun and already covered both ancestry and category.
items.cn: genus, generis 意为「出生、血统、族类、种类」，是第三变格法中性名词，本已兼指血统与类别。

items.en: The noun is tied to gignere 'to beget, bring forth', which also gives genius, generate and genital.
items.cn: 该名词与 gignere「生育、产生」相关，后者还给出 genius、generate 与 genital。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *ǵenh₁- 'to beget', also behind Greek genos and Latin gens; the reconstruction is conventional rather than attested.
items.cn: 更深词根被重构为 *ǵenh₁-「生育」，也见于希腊语 genos 与拉丁 gens；这一重构是通行做法，并非有据可查。

items.en: Before biology, genus named the wider class in the pair genus and species, a relation of containment.
items.cn: 在生物学之前，genus 指属种对中的上位类别，是一种包含关系。

items.en: Linnaeus placed genus immediately above species in the eighteenth century and made its name the first word of the binomial.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪把属置于种之上，并让属名成为双名法的第一个词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the exact English first use is not fixed here, and the pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：genus 最早的英语使用此处无法确定；拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words that look like genus but are not the same noun; group two compares the ranks and relations around it.
note.cn: 第一组区分看似 genus 却并非同一名词的词；第二组比较它周围的阶元与关系。

entries.definition: Inborn talent or a guiding spirit, from Latin genius 'attendant spirit', tied to gignere. It shares the root but is not the taxonomic rank.
entries.definitionCN: 天生的才能或守护神，来自拉丁 genius「守护灵」，与 gignere 相关。它共用词根，但不是分类阶元。

entries.definition: Authentic, from Latin genuinus 'natural, native'. It looks close but does not descend from genus.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的、地道的，来自拉丁 genuinus「天然的、本生的」。外形相近，却不出自 genus。

entries.definition: The Latin plural of genus, required in technical writing. It is the same word in another number, not another concept.
entries.definitionCN: genus 的拉丁复数，技术写作中必须使用。它是同一个词的另一种数，而非另一个概念。

entries.definition: The case of possession, from the same Latin stock but naming a grammatical function rather than a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 表示所属的格，出自同一拉丁词源，却指语法功能而非分类阶元。

entries.definition: The basic rank contained within a genus; the second word of a binomial.
entries.definitionCN: 包含在属之内的基本阶元；双名法的第二个词。

entries.definition: The rank above genus, grouping several genera that share a deeper common ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 属之上的阶元，把共享更深共同祖先的若干属聚合起来。

entries.definition: Any named group at any rank. A genus is one kind of taxon, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 任一阶元上被命名的类群。属是分类单元的一种，而非其同义词。

entries.definition: The genus that names and fixes a family; it is a role a genus can play, not a separate rank.
entries.definitionCN: 为科命名并固定其范围的那个属；它是属可以担任的角色，不是另一个阶元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genus comes from gignere 'to beget': a genus is a kind traced to a common birth.
normal.cn: genus 出自 gignere「生育」：一个属就是可追溯到共同出生的一类。

normal.en: The plural is genera, and the codes require it; genuses is a sign of amateur use.
normal.cn: 复数是 genera，法规要求如此；genuses 是外行的标志。

normal.en: The binomial is genus plus species epithet, as in Panthera leo.
normal.cn: 双名法是属名加种加词，如 Panthera leo。

normal.en: A family is named after its type genus, which anchors the name.
normal.cn: 科以模式属命名，模式属因此成为名称的锚。

normal.en: Generic drifted from 'of a genus' to 'common to a class' to 'unbranded'.
normal.cn: generic 从「属的」漂移到「整类共有的」，再漂移到「无品牌的」。

abstract.en: Picture a street name that covers many houses, each with its own number.
abstract.cn: 想象一个街名覆盖许多房子，每座房子有自己的门牌号。

abstract.en: Picture a family name shared by cousins who would not recognize each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一个姓氏被彼此不认识的表亲共用。

abstract.en: Picture a box marked 'kind of kinds', holding smaller boxes also marked that way.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写着「类之类」的盒子，里面装着同样标注的小盒子。

examples.en: The genus was split when molecular data showed two unrelated lineages.
examples.cn: 当分子数据显出两条无关谱系时，这个属被拆分了。

examples.en: After the first mention, the genus name is abbreviated to one letter.
examples.cn: 首次提及之后，属名缩写为一个字母。

examples.en: In the old logic, genus and species were relations, not organisms.
examples.cn: 在旧逻辑中，属与种是关系，而不是生物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gen 生 + us 我们」——同一个根生出来的一群 → genus 属

root: 拉丁 genus, generis「出生、族类、种类」，与 gignere「生育」相关；复数为 genera。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of genus move from the rank itself to its place in a binomial, its logical past, its everyday breadth, its Latin plural, the type genus, the monotypic case and finally the drift visible in generic.
sensesIntro.cn: genus 的八个义项从阶元本身出发，依次是双名法中的位置、逻辑学的前身、日常的宽度、拉丁复数、模式属、单型属，最后是 generic 中可见的语义漂移。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named box of kinds, sitting inside a larger box and holding smaller ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着各种「类」的命名盒子，它本身在更大的盒子里，又装着更小的盒子。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS ADDRESS: the genus is both a level and the street half of a binomial.
branches.cn: 阶元与地址：属既是一个层级，也是双名法地址中的街道部分。

branches.en: LOGIC AND EVERYDAY USE: containment and 'a kind of' keep the pre-biological meaning alive.
branches.cn: 逻辑与日常：包含关系与「一类」使生物学之前的意义继续存活。

branches.en: THE FORM: the Latin plural genera is obligatory in technical prose.
branches.cn: 形式：技术文献中必须使用拉丁复数 genera。

branches.en: ANCHOR AND EDGE CASE: the type genus fixes a family name, and a monotypic genus adds no information.
branches.cn: 锚点与边界情形：模式属固定科名，单型属则不增加信息。

branches.en: THE DERIVED DRIFT: generic moved from 'of a genus' to 'shared by a class' to 'unbranded'.
branches.cn: 派生漂移：generic 从「属的」变为「整类共有的」，再变为「无品牌的」。

intro.en: Genus is one Latin noun with a double life: a word for birth and lineage, and a word for a kind that contains kinds.
intro.cn: genus 是一个有双重生命的拉丁名词：既指出生与血统，也指容纳更小种类的种类。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus gives genus, genera, generic, generate, generation, genius and genital; gignere is the verb behind them all.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus 给出 genus、genera、generic、generate、generation、genius、genital；gignere 是它们背后的动词。

items.example: Genus is both a lineage word and a category word.
items.exampleCN: genus 既是血统词，也是类别词。

items.example: The verb supplies the sense of common birth.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「共同出生」的意思。

items.example: Three genera share the family.
items.exampleCN: 三个属共享这个科。

items.meaning: of a genus; common to a class
items.example: The generic name appears on the label.
items.exampleCN: 标签上写着属名。

items.example: The same root produced generate and generation.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根产生 generate 与 generation。

items.example: Genius is a cousin, not a synonym of genus.
items.exampleCN: genius 是远亲，而非 genus 的同义词。

items.example: Gens names a human lineage, not a taxonomic rank.
items.exampleCN: gens 指人的血统群体，而非分类阶元。

items.example: Greek genesis is a cousin through the same ancient root.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 genesis 经同一古老词根成为远亲。

definition_zh: 地理学家；研究地理的人
definition_en: a person who studies geography, especially its spatial patterns, environments, or maps
core_image: 一位背着测量仪的人沿河谷行走，边看地形边记录
scene: 一位研究者背着测量仪沿河谷行走，每到一处就记录河道宽度与坡度： A geographer walked the valley, recording the width and slope of the river.
sceneCN: 这里 geographer 指「研究地理的人；地理学家」（第 1 个义项：以地理学为业的人）；句意为一位地理学家沿河谷行走，记录河宽与坡度。

pos.zh: 地理学家；地理研究者（可数，复数为 geographers）

senses.title: A person who studies geography
senses.definition: a scholar or professional whose field is the study of places, environments, and spatial patterns
senses.definitionCN: 以地方、环境与空间格局为研究领域的学者或专业人员
senses.example: A geographer walked the valley, recording the width and slope of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一位地理学家沿河谷行走，记录河宽与坡度。
senses.why: The -er ending marks the practitioner, so geographer is simply 'one who does geography'.
senses.whyCN: -er 结尾标记从业者，因此 geographer 就是「做地理学的人」。

senses.title: A physical geographer
senses.definition: a geographer who studies landforms, climate, water, soils, or ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 研究地貌、气候、水、土壤或生态系统的地理学家
senses.example: The physical geographer measured how the glacier had retreated.
senses.exampleCN: 这位自然地理学家测量了冰川退缩的距离。
senses.why: The field divides, and each specialist carries the parent job title with an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 学科分支化后，每位专家都在母职称前加一个形容词。

senses.title: A historical mapmaker
senses.definition: an early geographer whose work was chiefly describing coasts and drawing maps
senses.definitionCN: 工作主要是描述海岸与绘制地图的早期地理工作者
senses.example: The geographer drew a coast that later explorers corrected.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地理学家画出的海岸线后来被探险者修正。
senses.why: Before geography became a university science, its practitioners were often mapmakers and compilers.
senses.whyCN: 在地理学成为大学科学之前，其实践者往往是制图者与编纂者。

senses.title: A human geographer
senses.definition: a geographer who studies cities, economies, cultures, or migration
senses.definitionCN: 研究城市、经济、文化或迁移的地理学家
senses.example: The human geographer interviewed families who had moved inland.
senses.exampleCN: 这位人文地理学家访谈了迁往内陆的家庭。
senses.why: People also make spatial patterns, so the same job title covers the study of settlements and movement.
senses.whyCN: 人同样制造空间格局，因此同一职称也涵盖聚落与迁移研究。

senses.title: A regional describer
senses.definition: someone who systematically describes the lands, peoples, and resources of a region
senses.definitionCN: 系统描述某一地区土地、人群与资源的人
senses.example: The geographer wrote a full account of the province's rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地理学家写下了该省河流的完整记述。
senses.why: The oldest sense is descriptive: to write down what is there, region by region.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是描述性的：一个地区一个地区地写下那里有什么。

senses.title: A geography teacher
senses.definition: a teacher who instructs students in geography
senses.definitionCN: 向学生教授地理学的教师
senses.example: The geographer at the school ran the map club.
senses.exampleCN: 学校里的地理老师负责地图社团。
senses.why: A discipline's name plus -er can also name the person who teaches it, especially in school usage.
senses.whyCN: 学科名加 -er 也可指教授它的人，尤其在学校语境中。

senses.title: A GIS or remote-sensing specialist
senses.titleCN: 地理信息系统或遥感专业人员
senses.definition: a geographer whose work uses satellite data, digital maps, and spatial analysis
senses.definitionCN: 使用卫星数据、数字地图与空间分析工作的地理学家
senses.example: The geographer turned satellite images into a flood-risk map.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地理学家把卫星影像转成洪水风险图。
senses.why: New instruments change the job while the old title stays, so geographer now includes digital mapping.
senses.whyCN: 新工具改变工作内容，旧职称却保留，因此地理学家如今也包括数字制图。

senses.title: Figurative: a person who knows a place
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：熟悉某地格局的人
senses.definition: someone who understands the layout and social map of a place very well
senses.definitionCN: 非常了解某地布局与社会地图的人
senses.example: As a geographer of the city, she knew every shortcut and every border.
senses.exampleCN: 作为熟悉这座城市的人，她知道每条捷径与每条边界。
senses.why: The metaphor promotes anyone with deep spatial knowledge to the rank of a geographer.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把任何具备深厚空间知识的人提升到「地理学家」的位置。

intro.en: Geographer comes from Greek through Latin, meaning 'one who writes about the earth'. The elements are clear; the deeper origin of ge is not. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geographer 经拉丁语来自希腊语，意为「书写大地的人」。语素清楚，但 ge 的更深来源不明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Geographos meant 'one who describes the earth', built on ge 'earth' and graphein 'to write'.
items.cn: geographos 意为「描述大地的人」，由 ge「大地」与 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: The element ge is of uncertain origin and is often regarded as pre-Greek; any Indo-European root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 语素 ge 来源不确定，常被视为前希腊语词；为它提出的任何印欧词根都属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed geographus for a writer on geography, and English took the word through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 geographus 指地理著述者，英语在 16 世纪经法语借入。

items.en: As geography became a university subject, geographer shifted from a writer of descriptions to a trained researcher.
items.cn: 随着地理学成为大学学科，geographer 从描述写作者转为受过训练的研究者。

items.en: Satellite and digital mapping added new roles in the twentieth century; the first use of geographer for these specialists is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 卫星与数字制图在 20 世纪增添了新角色，地理学家用于指这些专家的最早年代没有精确记载。

note.en: Group one holds job and subject words from the same Greek stock; group two holds specialists in neighbouring fields.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语词干的职业与学科词；第二组是相邻领域的专家。

entries.definition: The field itself; geographer is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；geographer 是从事它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to geography; it modifies nouns but does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与地理学有关；它修饰名词，但不指人。

entries.definition: The fuller adjective variant; it never replaces the noun for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 较长的形容词变体；它不能替代指人的名词。

entries.definition: The study of rocks and earth structure; its practitioner is a geologist, not a geographer.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石与地球结构的学科；其从业者是 geologist，而非 geographer。

entries.definition: A person who designs and draws maps; many geographers map, but cartography is a distinct skill.
entries.definitionCN: 设计并绘制地图的人；许多地理学家会制图，但制图是一门独立技能。

entries.definition: A person who studies rocks, minerals, and the earth's interior rather than surface places.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石、矿物与地球内部而非地表地方的人。

entries.definition: A person who measures land boundaries and elevations; the work supplies data that geographers use.
entries.definitionCN: 测量土地边界与高程的人；其工作为地理学家提供数据。

entries.definition: A person who travels into unknown regions; early explorers often supplied geography with its descriptions.
entries.definitionCN: 进入未知地区旅行的人；早期探险者常为地理学提供描述材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real professions and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊语素、真实职业与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Geography is the field; geographer is the person; geographic is the adjective.
normal.cn: geography 是学科，geographer 是人，geographic 是形容词。

normal.en: The -er ending marks the practitioner, as in teacher and mapper.
normal.cn: -er 结尾标记从业者，如 teacher 与 mapper。

normal.en: A geographer may be physical, human, economic, or digital.
normal.cn: 地理学家可以是自然的、人文的、经济的或数字的。

normal.en: Early geographers were often mapmakers and regional describers.
normal.cn: 早期地理学家往往是制图者与区域描述者。

normal.en: The Greek source geographos literally means earth-writer.
normal.cn: 希腊语来源 geographos 字面就是「书写大地的人」。

abstract.en: Picture a person who carries a map in the head instead of the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把地图装在心里，而不是拿在手上。

abstract.en: Picture someone who can feel a border before seeing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人还没看见边界，就能感觉到它。

abstract.en: Picture a guide whose directions are really a description of the land.
abstract.cn: 想象一位向导，他的指路其实是对大地的描述。

examples.en: A geographer walked the valley, recording the width and slope of the river.
examples.cn: 一位地理学家沿河谷行走，记录河宽与坡度。

examples.en: The geographer compared rainfall records from a hundred stations.
examples.cn: 这位地理学家比较了一百个站点的降水记录。

examples.en: A human geographer studied how the new road changed village life.
examples.cn: 一位人文地理学家研究了新公路如何改变村庄生活。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「geo（大地）+ grapher（书写者）」——书写大地的人 → 地理学家

root: 拉丁语 geographus，来自希腊语 geographos = ge「大地」+ graphein「书写」+ -os（人）。ge 更深来源不确定；graphein 词根清楚。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general practitioner to physical and human specialists, historical mapmakers, regional describers, teachers, digital specialists, and finally to anyone who knows a place deeply.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般从业者走到自然与人文专家、历史制图者、区域描述者、教师、数字专家，最后落到任何深谙某地的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person walking a valley with instruments, writing down what the land does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人带着仪器走在河谷里，记录大地的表现。

branches.en: RESEARCHER AND TEACHER: the same title covers those who advance the field and those who teach it.
branches.cn: 研究者与教师：同一职称既指推进学科的人，也指教授它的人。

branches.en: TWO BRANCHES: physical and human geographers split the living surface between them.
branches.cn: 两个分支：自然与人文地理学家把活的地表一分为二。

branches.en: DESCRIPTION AND MAP: the oldest tasks were writing down regions and drawing their coasts.
branches.cn: 描述与地图：最古老的任务是记述区域与描画海岸。

branches.en: NEW INSTRUMENTS: satellites and digital maps extend the craft without renaming it.
branches.cn: 新工具：卫星与数字地图扩展了技艺，却未改变职称。

branches.en: METAPHOR: deep knowledge of a place is treated as a professional qualification.
branches.cn: 比喻：对某地的深刻了解被当作一种专业资格。

intro.en: Geographer is a Greek compound plus the English agent suffix -er, so its structure is easy to read.
intro.cn: geographer 是希腊语复合词加英语施事后缀 -er，结构容易读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin geographus is the borrowed intermediate; Greek ge and graphein are the ultimate elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 geographus 是借入的中间形式；希腊语 ge 与 graphein 是最终语素。

items.example: Ge- marks earth sciences.
items.exampleCN: ge- 标记地球科学。

items.example: -Grapher appears in geographer and photographer.
items.exampleCN: -grapher 见于 geographer 与 photographer。

items.example: Geography is what the geographer practises.
items.exampleCN: 地理学是地理学家从事的学问。

items.example: The geographer mapped the old river channels.
items.exampleCN: 这位地理学家标绘了古河道。

items.example: The geographer used geographic data.
items.exampleCN: 这位地理学家使用了地理数据。

items.example: The society publishes geographical research.
items.exampleCN: 该学会出版地理研究。

items.example: The two sites are geographically close.
items.exampleCN: 两处地点在地理上很近。

items.meaningCN: 研究岩石的学科；地质学
items.example: A geologist, not a geographer, studies deep rock.
items.exampleCN: 研究深部岩石的是地质学家，而非地理学家。

items.example: Cartographers turn survey data into maps.
items.exampleCN: 制图者把测量数据变成地图。
